Foreign-born athletes won 19 of 22 Asian Games medals for Bahrain. They’re from Africa, Russia & beyond

From Kenya and Ethiopia to Nigeria, Egypt and Sudan, several athletes born outside the two Gulf nations have won medals for their adopted countries in Japan.

Pakhi Khare

05 October, 2026 09:41 pm IST

Facebook

Twitter

WhatsApp

Linkedin

Qatar's Bassem Hemeida won gold in men's 400m hurdles, while Bahrain's Birhanu Balew successfully defended his men's 5000m title by coming first. Both athletes are from Africa | X/@AsianGamesOCA

Follow Us :

Text Size: A- A+

-->

New Delhi: With 22 medals including 11 gold, Bahrain finished top among Arab countries at the just concluded 2026 Asian Games. The country came 10th in the final medal tally. What’s eye-catching is the fact that as many as 19 of them were clinched by foreign-born athletes, primarily from Africa, in individual events.

Their home countries range from Kenya, Ethiopia to Nigeria, Egypt, and Sudan. A case in point is the Ethiopia-born Birhanu Balew who successfully defended his titles by winning gold medals in the men’s 5000m and 10,000m events at the recent 20th Asian Games in Aichi-Nagoya.

The long-distance runner finalised his transfer of sporting allegiance to represent Bahrain in 2014, the year when he got Bahrain citizenship. He was cleared to play for Bahrain in international games starting from 8th October 2015, according to the World Athletics record.

Show Full Article

Another such athlete is Kenya-born Winfred Yavi, who won a record three individual gold medals in women’s 10,000m, women’s 3,000m steeplechase, and women’s 5,000 m.

Yavi had changed her sporting allegiance when she was a teenager. She was eligible to represent Bahrain from 19 August 2016, according to World Athletics .

In a 2023 interview to The Star , the Kenyan-born Olympic record holder conceded that she opted for Bahrain after she was unable to find a place in the home team owing to stiff competition. She further added that she has gotten Bahraini nationality.

"I didn't get the opportunity to represent Kenya," says the Women's 3000m Steeplechase Paris Olympic gold medalist, Winfred Mutile Yavi explaining her decision to run for Bahrain instead of Kenya. #Olympics pic.twitter.com/M98cSOXFEX

— Ole Teya (@TeyaKevin) August 6, 2024

Similarly, middle-distance runner Nelly Korir won gold and silver in 1500 m and 800 m respectively. According to the World Athletics Records, she was representing Kenya until 31 March 2017 and later cleared to represent Bahrain starting from 13 August 2021.

Other such cases include runners Salwa Naser (gold in women’s 400m) and Shitaye Habte (gold in women’s marathon). Naser was born in Anambra State, Nigeria, but moved to Bahrain at 14 seeking opportunities to further her running career, the BBC reported. Habte was born in Ethiopia.

But it is not just from Africa. Swimmer Mikhail Arkhangelskiy (gold in men’s 50 butterfly) and MMA fighter Diana Pogosian (silver in the women under-54kg category) swapped their allegiance from Russia to Bahrain.

Arkhangelskiy was born to political refugees who fled Russia for France. “If I go back to Russia, I’ll be arrested because my family are political opponents,” he was quoted as saying by Reuters .

Wrestler and bronze medalist Sharipov Shamil is originally from Dagestan, Russia. MMA fighter Mukhammad Nabiev, who won silver in men’s traditional 77kg, is also from Russia. Weightlifter Alinary Marushchak, a silver medalist in the women’s 86 kg category, is from Ukraine.

Sprinter Edidiong Odiong (Nigeria), distance runner Albert Kiptoo (Kenya), judoka Sukhrob Boqiev (Tajikistan), weightlifters Gor Minasayan (Armenia) and Ingrid Grueso (Colombia)—all bronze medalists—took the same route to represent Bahrain.

This practice is not new in international sport, and both Bahrain as well as Qatar over the years have had such sportspersons in their contingents in international multi-sport events.

Way back in 2008, Time magazine had called the two countries as “the gold medalists in recruiting foreign-born athletes”. These “tiny oil-rich Gulf states”, it added, have “poached top runners from Kenya, Morocco, and Ethiopia”. The article goes on to mention that the trend began in the 1990s, when Saif Saeed Asaad, formerly Angel Popov, a Bulgarian weightlifter, switched allegiance to Qatar.

Qatar ended with 18 medals including 6 gold in the 20th Asian Games. Its overall standing was 14th in the medal tally. The Gulf country will be hosting the next edition of the Asian Games in Doha in 2030.

Egypt-born Bassem Hemeida won gold and silver in men’s 400m hurdle and 4x400m relay, respectively. His Asian Games athlete profile says that he decided to represent Qatar in 2016.

陸上競技 男子400mハードル！🔥

金メダルのHEMEIDA Bassem選手(カタール)が見せた圧巻のラストスパート！！🥇

銀メダルの後藤大樹選手(日本)は、この種目において国内史上最年少で表彰台に上りました👏 #アジア競技大会 #愛知名古屋2026 pic.twitter.com/2ilgOzvzTx

— 第20回アジア競技大会(2026/愛知・名古屋) (@AsianGames_2026) October 1, 2026

Similarly, Sudan-born Abubanker Haydar Abdalla got a bronze in men’s 800m. The middle-distance runner had previously won bronze at the 2018 Asian Games in Jakarta. Another such athlete is middle-distance runner Zakaria Ibrahim Elahlaami (bronze in the men’s 3000m steeplechase), who became eligible to represent Qatar in January 2024.

In wrestling, Greco-Roman wrestler Shahin Badaghimofrad made history by winning Qatar’s first-ever gold medal at the Asian Wrestling Championships.

The United World Wrestling report describes Badaghimofrad as “Iranian-born” and that he was competing for Iran when he first appeared at the Asian Championships. It adds that he changed his allegiance after 2023 and made his debut for Qatar in February 2025.

This is an updated version of the article.

(Edited by Tony Rai)

Ex Anthropic researcher who warned AI may become too powerful to control to testify at NYC hearing

Jacob Coxon will appear at request of Council Speaker Julie Menin, who's urged AI whistleblowers to testify as city lawmakers weigh a package of bills aimed at establishing safeguards.

Nacha Cattan  and  Laura Nahmias

05 October, 2026 09:25 pm IST

Facebook

Twitter

WhatsApp

Linkedin

An Anthropic PBC artificial intelligence (AI) logo on a smartphone arranged in Riga, Latvia, on Wednesday, July 1, 2026. Washingtons opaque restrictions on who can use these tools have highlighted how heavily the digital security of many US allies depends on American policy. | Bloomberg

Follow Us :

Text Size: A- A+

-->

Former Anthropic researcher Jacob Coxon, who warned that artificial intelligence could become too powerful for humans to control, will testify Monday at a New York City Council hearing alongside representatives of some of the world’s biggest AI companies.

Coxon will appear at the request of Council Speaker Julie Menin, who has urged AI whistleblowers to testify as city lawmakers weigh a package of bills aimed at establishing safeguards around the technology, according to people familiar with the matter.

Coxon quit Anthropic last month and issued a stark warning about the race to develop increasingly powerful AI, accusing his former employer and OpenAI of “gambling with our lives.” He confirmed he plans to testify on Monday.

Show Full Article

The hearing will put some of the industry’s most vocal critics in the same room as representatives of Anthropic, OpenAI, Alphabet Inc.’s Google and Meta Platforms Inc.

Former Google DeepMind researcher Alex Turner and Daniel Kokotajlo, executive director of the AI Futures Project and a former OpenAI researcher, are also expected to testify, according to one of the people. Turner confirmed he plans to attend the hearing. Kokotajlo couldn’t be reached for comment.

Menin’s office said Anthropic will be represented by Logan Graham, head of its Frontier Red Team, which tests advanced AI models for their capabilities and risks. OpenAI will send Morgan Dwyer, head of policy development and operations; Meta will send Shane Cahill, an AI policy director; and Google will be represented by AI policy executive Alice Friend.

A spokesperson for Google declined to comment. Representatives for the other companies didn’t respond to requests for comment.

The hearing is part of an effort by New York officials to play a larger role in regulating an industry that has expanded rapidly in the city even as much of AI regulation remains the province of federal and state governments.

One proposal before the council, sponsored by Menin, would give whistleblowers a portion of fines or penalties recovered from AI companies following reported violations. Other legislation under consideration would allow people harmed by AI systems to sue developers under certain circumstances and require third-party validation of some systems before they can be deployed in the city.

OpenAI, Anthropic and Google agreed to appear after Menin’s office warned that they could be subpoenaed, while Meta had committed to attending earlier, Bloomberg News previously reported. The Council subpoenaed SpaceX’s artificial intelligence unit after it failed to respond to requests to appear.

Officials from Mayor Zohran Mamdani’s administration will also testify, including Samuel Levine, commissioner of the Department of Consumer and Worker Protection, and Sarah Milstein, deputy commissioner at the Office of Technology and Innovation.

US-India trade deal talks at a ‘plateau’, Finance minister Nirmala Sitharaman says

Sitharaman’s comments follow those of US Trade Representative Jamieson Greer that a trade deal is in its final stages, but not ‘imminent.’

Shruti Srivastava

05 October, 2026 05:15 pm IST

Facebook

Twitter

WhatsApp

Linkedin

Nirmala Sitharaman, India's finance minister, during the Global Fintech Fest in Mumbai, India, on Friday, 11 Sept, 2026. | Photographer: Dhiraj Singh/Bloomberg

Follow Us :

Text Size: A- A+

-->

Top officials in the US and India signaled that negotiations over a trade deal have reached an impasse that’s making it difficult to clinch an agreement.

Indian Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman said Monday that talks have “reached a plateau” beyond which a compromise would be difficult. That followed comments from United State Trade Representative Jamieson Greer on Friday that a trade deal was in its final stages, but not “imminent.”

The two sides agreed to an interim deal earlier this year and have been locked in negotiations ever since. Indian officials have sought assurances from the US that the country would have a favorable tariff rate over its peers and that it wouldn’t face additional penalties once the trade deal is signed.

Show Full Article

Speaking at the Munich Security Conference on Monday, Sitharaman said trade negotiations have been difficult and rigorous, and “we would like to believe that both sides have reached a plateau beyond which giving or taking might be very, very difficult.”

“Maybe if there are rooms to operate from, both sides would do it,” she said.

The talks have been complicated by new US legislation giving President Donald Trump the ability to impose tariffs of as much as 100% on the top buyers of Russian oil and gas. India, a major importer of Russian energy, has warned that such measures could hurt bilateral ties with the US and disrupt global energy markets.

US-India ties have come under strain in the past 18 months, with Trump imposing punitive tariffs on India for buying Russian oil, before removing them. The US leader has repeatedly claimed he’d helped mediate a ceasefire to end a brief armed conflict between India and Pakistan in May 2025. New Delhi has consistently rejected Trump’s version of events.

Trump and Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi held their first phone call since June last week, discussing trade and energy, as well as defense and critical minerals.

‘Lonelier Power’

India’s External Affairs Minister Subrahmanyam Jaishankar on Sunday warned that the US was becoming increasingly isolated in the new global order.

“Nobody would disagree with the fact that the landscape today is primarily marked by a radical repositioning of the United States,” he said at the Munich Security Conference. “A repositioning which is a posture of choice, and where it has deliberately become a lonelier power.”

Rising competition between the US and China have also led to the “weaponization of any leverage that any country has,” he said.

Indian Commerce and Industry Minister Piyush Goyal held what he described as “productive talks” with Greer in Milwaukee on the sidelines of the Group of 20 trade ministers’ meeting last week.

Greer said on Friday officials were working to iron out their disputes.

“I would characterize and say we are in the short strokes,” Greer said. The two sides have identified the “universe of items that are sticking points, and we are working diligently toward them,” he said.

US accuses California woman of spying for China, surveilling Taiwan president’s son

Reuters

05 October, 2026 09:00 am IST

Facebook

Twitter

WhatsApp

Linkedin

(c) Copyright Thomson Reuters 2026

Follow Us :

Text Size: A- A+

-->

By Kanishka Singh WASHINGTON, Oct 4 (Reuters) – US authorities arrested a California woman on Sunday and accused her of spying on a son of Taiwan’s president at the behest of Chinese officials, the FBI said.

The FBI arrested Wanying Zhang, also known as Heather, at Los Angeles International Airport on Sunday before her planned departure to China, the agency said in a statement. Authorities charged Zhang, 34, of Irvine, California, with acting as an unregistered foreign agent.

Zhang surveilled a son of Taiwanese President Lai Ching-te, the FBI said. The agency did not directly name Zhang’s alleged target, but later shared a New York Post report identifying him as Lai Ting-yu, a US resident.

Show Full Article

Taiwan’s presidential office described Zhang’s actions as a “typical case of transnational repression” and thanked the US government for protecting Taiwanese citizens.

“Our country expresses the strongest condemnation of such barbaric conduct that disregards human rights and the sovereignty of nations,” spokesperson Karen Kuo said in a statement.

China’s foreign ministry did not respond to a request for comment.

Lai and his Democratic Progressive Party champion Taiwan’s separate identity from China, a position that frequently angers Beijing, which views the island as Chinese territory. Lai says only Taiwan’s people can decide their future.

The Justice Department said Zhang traveled to Seattle in 2025 at the direction of Chinese officials and sent them photos, video and license plate information of the Taiwanese president’s son and his family.

Zhang used tradecraft to avoid detection and never notified Washington that she was acting for a foreign government, Bill Essayli, the first assistant US attorney for the Central District of California, said in a statement.

It was not immediately clear whether Zhang has a defense attorney. She will appear on Monday in a Los Angeles federal court, Essayli said.

Washington does not have formal diplomatic ties with Taiwan, but the United States is the island’s most important international backer and weapons supplier.

(Reporting by Kanishka Singh in Washington; Additional reporting by Ben Blanchard in Taipei and Joe Cash in Beijing; Editing by Sergio Non and Edwina Gibbs)
